title: [C14T1] - Average percentages in typical meals
prompt: The charts below show the average percentages in typical meals of three types of nutrients, all of which may be unhealthy if eaten too much. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts provide information about the average proportions of three types of nutrients - sodium, saturated fat, and added sugar - consumed during different meals throughout a typical day in the USA.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, dinner accounts for the largest proportion of sodium and saturated fat intake, while snacks contribute the most to added sugar consumption. In contrast, breakfast consistently represents the smallest percentage across all three nutrient categories.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding sodium and saturated fat consumption, dinner is the primary contributor to both nutrients, accounting for 43% of sodium intake and 37% of saturated fat consumption. Lunch represents the second-highest source for both nutrients, providing 29% of daily sodium and 26% of saturated fat. Meanwhile, breakfast contributes equally to both nutrients at 14%, while snacks provide a similar 14% of sodium but a notably higher 21% of saturated fat.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for added sugar consumption, the pattern differs significantly, with snacks being the dominant source at 42% of total intake. Dinner contributes 23% of added sugar, while breakfast and lunch account for smaller and nearly equal proportions at 16% and 19% respectively.
